task: Close untyped domain handler and state inference gaps found in a bounded C++/Java checker comparison.
observation: The first 50 sorted top-level Moss fixtures had 49 C++ acceptances and 44 Java acceptances. Java incorrectly rejected uniform untyped handler/state cases, and a bounded inference pass now makes three of those fixtures pass checking and Fast Debug with output matching C++. The refreshed check-only sample has 49 C++ acceptances and 47 Java acceptances; the two remaining disagreements use distinct inferred layouts for separate instances of one source domain, which requires per-instance specialization rather than a shared declaration type. A follow-on checker/backend pass now materializes separate concrete domain declarations for closed, route-free instances constructed directly in main, and rewrites later constructors to their specialized declaration. The two formerly rejected positive fixtures now check and produce matching Fast Debug output. Existing same-instance conflicting-layout fixtures are rejected by both compilers with MOSS_COMPILE_ERROR.
impact: The bounded sample now has matching acceptance results: C++ and Java each accept 49 of 50 files, with no acceptance mismatches. Four focused negative conflicts also reject in both compilers. This only covers direct main-scope, route-free, non-exported domains without state initializers; native Rust compilation and broader domain shapes remain unverified.

resolution.summary: Added per-instance concrete layouts for the tested direct-main route-free cases and conflict diagnostics; routed, initialized, exported, nested/control-flow, and native lowering coverage remain open.
